results.quote: Six forms on the chute: form 1 under the hopper, form 6 at the end.
Mix counts in whole units. (never-negative is not stated)
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Every form starts GREEN. ... Starting mix: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Washout limit: 38 ... go on the loss tally, starting at zero.
Five cycles, five steps each, in this order. Each step finishes on all six forms before the next.
Pour. Each form takes its units, even past capacity.
Go form 1 to form 6, one at a time. Anything over capacity runs into the next form down; the form is left exactly full.
Form 1's overtop is already in form 2 when you reach it, so it can cascade.
Form 6 overtops into the waste pit.
State check, on what's in the forms now. GREEN at or above the upper mark goes HOT.
HOT at or below the lower mark goes back to GREEN
Anything else keeps its state. One change per form per cycle at most.
Figure all six amounts from current contents first, then move them together.
GREEN loses a quarter, rounded down, to evaporation: waste.
HOT bleeds half, rounded down, back up the chute into the form before it (5 into 4). Form 1's bleed is waste.
A form can bleed and receive in the same step. No capacity limit: overfill waits for next cycle's overtop, and after cycle 5 it stays.
Total all six. Strictly over 38: ... Otherwise nothing.
each form keeps half, rounded down; the rest is waste; note the cycle.

the six end quantities, positions 1 to 6; the six end states; every state change as (cycle, position, before, after); the cycles the washout fired; the loss tally; and the balance check: starting mix plus all pours must equal end quantities plus loss tally.
